summary: Redwood walkthrough of data handling and retention controls focused on logging redaction, PII removal, request storage toggles in API and Console. Sable asked about retention limits, KMS integration, audit logs, and a 24h perf trial. Next steps: security docs, screenshots, trial tenant provisioning.
transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, uh we're gonna focus today on our data handling and retention controls, logging redaction and how you can toggle request storage both via API and the console.
00:07 Maya Ortiz: thanks Alex, appreciate it. we're particularly concerned about transaction-level data and PCI adjacent info. we want to be sure nothing PII-ish is stored by the default API.
00:15 Alex Chen: totally, that's core to the demo. quick intros — i'm Alex (AE), Priya (SE) will run the console demo, and you all?
00:22 Maya Ortiz: Maya, Head of Payments. Daniel security, Priya platform.
00:26 Priya Rao: great, i'll share my screen, give me a sec. okay seeing the Redwood console. i'm gonna jump to the Project Settings > Data Controls section.
00:40 Priya Rao: so first row is request storage — default for hosted is "store requests for 30 days" for analytics, but you can change that per-project. there are three toggles: store-full-requests, store-metadata-only, and no-storage.
00:54 Daniel Kim: when you say store-metadata-only what does metadata include? request id, model, token counts?
01:01 Priya Rao: yes exactly — request id, model version, latency, token counts, route, and anonymized client-id. it explicitly strips request text. so the actual prompt content is not persisted in metadata-only mode.
01:12 Daniel Kim: and is that flow enforced server-side or is that client-configurable flag? we need guarantees for audit.
01:18 Priya Rao: it's enforced server-side per-project. you set the project policy, and requests are ingested with a flag; the storage layer enforces redaction. for hosted customers we also surface an exportable audit log showing the policy applied to each request — not the content.
01:31 Maya Ortiz: can you show how to toggle redaction rules? we have card numbers sometimes in prompts, that's the main PII worry.
01:38 Priya Rao: sure. under Data Controls > Redaction Rules you can upload regex patterns or select prebuilt patterns: PII, PCI, SSN, email, phone. you can choose to do client-side masking (SDK) or server-side redaction. i'm going to enable server-side PCI redaction and show a simulated request.
01:55 Alex Chen: small note — server-side redaction runs in our ingestion pipeline before anything is persisted to request storage or logs; it also strips from streaming buffers and from any exportable logs.
02:05 Priya Singh: what about function/tool payloads? we send structured calls with sensitive fields.
02:10 Priya Rao: good question — you can mark specific JSON paths as secret in the console. those paths are nullified in stored requests and replaced with a redaction token in the console UI. during live inference the runtime will still pass the full field to the model if you choose, but it won't be stored or show up in logs.
02:28 Daniel Kim: is there an allowlist for who can turn off storage? we can't have non-security folks disabling retention.
02:33 Priya Rao: RBAC ties to SSO groups. only project admins and the security role can change retention policies. we also log policy changes to the audit log with the user, timestamp, and IP.
02:45 Maya Ortiz: demo the redaction — please paste a fake card number in a prompt.
02:48 Priya Rao: okay i'm going to call the API from the inline editor. payload: {
02:52 Priya Rao: prompt: "refund order 8273 confirm card 4111-1111-1111-1111"
03:00 Priya Rao: sending... response comes back, model replied: "refund initiated for order 8273" — you can see downstream we didn't echo the card. now check storage to confirm.
03:12 Priya Rao: navigating to Request Explorer, filter last 10 minutes, request shows prompt redacted: "refund order 8273 confirm card [REDACTED_PCI]". raw content is not available.
03:25 Daniel Kim: ok that's encouraging. what if we want zero retention at all, like ephemeral mode?
03:30 Alex Chen: we support a no-storage mode: nothing persists, no traces in request storage, no user-level logs. metric aggregation still happens for system health (we can provide aggregated telemetry only, not request-level), and you can choose to disable even aggregated telemetry for dedicated/private installs.
03:45 Maya Ortiz: for hosted customers, if we pick no-storage, can we still debug issues?
03:49 Alex Chen: you can enable debug snapshots for a rolling 1-hour window which are stored encrypted and access-controlled; snapshots are only available if explicitly enabled and will contain redacted content depending on policy.
03:58 Priya Singh: encryption at rest — do you integrate with customer KMS?
04:02 Priya Rao: yes, for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). for hosted we offer optional CMEK per-account — you provide the KMS ARN and we do envelope encryption.
04:13 Daniel Kim: how about key rotation and revocation?
04:16 Priya Rao: envelope keys in our storage layer mean you can rotate the underlying KMS key; we keep an access log for key usage. if you revoke the key you'd lose the ability to decrypt historical snapshots — we surface that as a risk in the console when you rotate.
04:28 Maya Ortiz: you mentioned audit logs — can they be forwarded to our SIEM?
04:31 Priya Rao: yes logs can be shipped to your CloudWatch/Datadog/Splunk via our integration or pulled with a secure export endpoint. the exported logs respect redaction policies — we never export full request content if redaction is enabled.
04:45 Daniel Kim: what's the retention delta across tiers? i.e. hosted default 30 days but can we do 7 or 0. Dedicated?
04:52 Alex Chen: hosted: configurable 0/7/30/90. Dedicated: you pick your own retention policy as part of the contract, including unlimited retention if you want. Private: entirely customer controlled.
05:02 Maya Ortiz: are there any compliance attestations for hosted with lower retention? do we need an annex?
05:07 Priya Rao: SOC2 Type II is standard; we can provide environment-specific reports for enterprise deals and a data processing addendum that limits retention and sets obligations.
05:17 Daniel Kim: API-wise is there a header we can pass per-request to opt-out of storage?
05:21 Priya Rao: yes there's an optional header x-redwood-storage: "no-store"|"metadata-only"|"store" that overrides project defaults. note: project admin can disable per-request overrides if you want uniform enforcement.
05:35 Priya Singh: great. how is PII detection done? ML-based detection or just regex?
05:40 Priya Rao: hybrid. we have prebuilt regexes for structured things like card numbers and SSNs and an ML detector for contextual PII which catches names/addresses. you can tune sensitivity and add allow/block lists.
05:52 Alex Chen: quick note — detectors run inline in the ingestion layer before model execution to prevent leaks to logs/exports.
05:58 Maya Ortiz: about streaming — if we stream tokens to the client, are tokens buffered anywhere?
06:03 Priya Rao: streaming buffers are ephemeral in the runtime and not persisted. however if you enable logging or debug snapshots they will contain the redacted stream based on policy.
06:14 Daniel Kim: curious about embeddings — when we send data for embeddings are the vectors stored by default? we use embeddings for search and would like control.
06:21 Priya Rao: embeddings storage is separate. by default we don't persist embeddings unless you opt-in to the vector DB. we provide a managed vectors option where you can choose TTLs and zero-retention, or you can export encrypted vectors to your own store.
06:34 Maya Ortiz: what about model fine-tuning or training with our data?
06:38 Alex Chen: Redwood does not use customer data for model training by default. If you opt into a managed fine-tuning program that's a separate contract with explicit data controls.
06:45 Daniel Kim: okay demo the API call header and show a sample curl?
06:48 Priya Rao: sure. curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "x-redwood-storage: no-store" -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
06:58 Priya Rao: when set to no-store you'll see a storage flag in the response metadata: {"storage_applied":"no-store"}. the console request explorer will show a request with storage_applied=no-store and no content.
07:12 Maya Ortiz: can we get per-team defaults for different services? some internal teams want 30 days, others 0.
07:18 Priya Rao: yep project-level settings support inherited policies from org-level and per-project overrides plus policy templates you can apply to groups of projects.
07:27 Daniel Kim: are redaction rules deterministic? e.g. will a masked card number always be replaced by [REDACTED_PCI] or sometimes by tokens?
07:33 Priya Rao: deterministic — policy defines the token format. by default [REDACTED_PCI] is used, but you can map to token IDs if you need deterministic pseudonyms for correlation. those token maps can be one-way hashed and stored encrypted.
07:47 Priya Singh: let's talk private deployment — if we run Redwood in our VPC, is the ingestion pipeline still your managed code or do we get the whole stack?
07:55 Alex Chen: for Private we ship the control plane (customer-managed control plane option). runtime and ingestion can run inside your VPC/on-prem. for full air-gapped we provide an appliance. in those cases you control KMS, logs, and retention entirely.
08:10 Maya Ortiz: latency-wise will redaction add measurable latency?
08:14 Priya Rao: redaction adds minimal overhead — regex checks are trivial; ML detectors run in parallel and usually add 10-30ms depending on payload size. we can run detectors asynchronously for non-blocking cases.
08:26 Daniel Kim: can we run our own detectors in the pipeline? we have a custom ML PII model.
08:30 Priya Rao: yes, for Dedicated/Private we support custom detector hooks via a secure sidecar. you can plug your model which runs before storage/escalation.
08:40 Maya Ortiz: okay show me how to export logs to Splunk with redaction preserved.
08:43 Priya Rao: heading to Integrations > Log exports > add destination > Splunk. configure endpoint and choose exported fields — selecting "redacted_requests" ensures content is not included. demo export test success.
08:58 Alex Chen: quick pause for timeline: you mentioned a 24h perf trial at approx 100 TPS — we can provision a sandbox with dedicated GPU capacity for that. we'll need your traffic profile and sample payloads.
09:10 Daniel Kim: i'll send sample payloads and target latencies.
09:13 Maya Ortiz: for pricing, does enabling CMEK or dedicated retention change costs?
09:18 Alex Chen: yes CMEK and dedicated retention are add-ons. we'll include those in the pricing doc. dedicated hardware priced by reserved capacity plus storage tiers.
09:27 Priya Singh: if an org admin disables per-request header overrides, is there a way for a dev to request temporary debug access?
09:32 Priya Rao: yes it's an approver flow — a request ticket goes to security owners, and if approved a one-time debug window (1hr) is granted and logged.
09:41 Maya Ortiz: what about cross-region data residency? our EU customers data needs to stay in eu-west-1.
09:46 Alex Chen: you can pin projects to regions; hosted will keep data and compute in the selected region. for Dedicated we can provision capacity in your target region. Private gives you full control.
09:58 Daniel Kim: do you have examples of redaction false positives/negatives? how do you measure detector quality?
10:03 Priya Rao: we provide evaluation reports with precision/recall on sample prompt sets. you can also submit your own dataset to run against our detectors. false positives can be tuned with allowlists.
10:12 Maya Ortiz: ok let's go through an example where the model outputs something that looks like a card — does Redwood scrub outputs too?
10:18 Priya Rao: yes output redaction is symmetrical — the output passes through the same detectors before any storage or logs. by default we scrub outputs for PII in stored records and debug snapshots.
10:29 Daniel Kim: what about cached KV in model serving — could that leak tokens across requests?
10:35 Alex Chen: KV cache is per-session and not persisted across sessions. we encrypt caches and they are cleared on session end. we also have an option to disable KV caching entirely for sensitive workloads.
10:48 Maya Ortiz: good. any limitations for webhooks or downstream integrations?
10:52 Priya Rao: webhooks receive the response as delivered to the client. if you've enabled no-store the webhook payload will not include stored content but will include the live response. webhook logs can be redacted on export.
11:04 Daniel Kim: can we run an automated regression suite to ensure redaction hasn't changed?
11:08 Priya Rao: yes our Optimize product has a monitoring runner where you can define prompt sets and assert that PII is not present in stored outputs. we can set alerts on regression.
11:20 Maya Ortiz: ok very helpful. couple more quick Qs — is there a papertrail for redaction rule changes? who edited regexes?
11:27 Priya Rao: yes full audit trail with diff of rule content, who edited, preview of impact on a sample set.
11:36 Alex Chen: we're approaching time — quick recap and next steps.
11:40 Alex Chen: recap: server-side and client-side redaction, per-project retention toggles, x-redwood-storage header, RBAC for policy changes, CMEK support, audit logs to SIEM, dedicated/private options for stricter controls, Optimize monitoring for regression alerts.
11:53 Maya Ortiz: next steps: we'll review security doc, we'll provide payload samples for the perf trial, and Daniel will create a short list of KMS endpoints and compliance questions.
12:02 Daniel Kim: yes i'll send those by Friday.
12:05 Alex Chen: perfect. Priya will share the recording and screenshots of the redaction flow.
12:09 Priya Rao: sending now, and i'll also include a sample curl and a small script that toggles x-redwood-storage per request.
12:16 Maya Ortiz: thanks everyone, this is great.
12:18 Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc and pricing. bye!
12:22 (call ended)
